content.text:
I published 2.3.0, and it's now the latest release: https://github.com/cv/pi-action/releases/tag/v2.3.0

Most of the release already existed, so I only finished the last step.
- Release PR #45 was merged as `12bf89d`, with `package.json` and `package-lock.json` set to 2.3.0.
- The `v2.3.0` tag was already on that commit. The release workflow run passed ([run](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/actions/runs/43192880631)): it checked the tag, ran `npm run check` and created the draft. It also moved `v2` to that commit, so `cv/pi-action@v2` users already had 2.3.0.
- The draft notes were there but had never been published. I published them as they were, without edits. They cover working-tree continuity, the new workflow log, and the fixes from #47.

**Not in 2.3.0:** two commits merged after the tag, so this release doesn't include them:
- `7c25709` feat: prompt templates, tool exclusion, and overrides from extensions (#56)
- `06084db` ci: offer the model only pit's typescript tool in pi-assistant (#58)

I didn't move `v2.3.0` to include them, because the tag was already pushed and `v2` users are already on it. Since #56 is a new feature, it fits a 2.4.0 release. Just ask (`@pi create a 2.4.0 release`) and I'll open the release PR with notes, following the process in CONTRIBUTING.md.

I didn't change any files, so there was nothing to commit.
